clue.text: Courses arranged by a man of vast means

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the word courses are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone very rich has had a series of courses laid out for him, like a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles COURSES into the name of the fabulously rich ancient king of Lydia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lydian king was proverbially wealthy, so his name stands for any immensely rich person.

clue.text: Tart dish

definitions.meaning: a prostitute, the French word used in English
a small ovenproof pot for one portion

explanation.surface: A pastry served on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: In French slang it means a loose woman, and it is also a small ramekin-like pan for baking eggs.

clue.text: Former point entered punctually

indicators.note: entered means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: on time means punctually
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: An earlier point was made exactly when expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts E (east, a compass point) into ON TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was once so but no longer is, like a past champion, is a previous one.

clue.text: Authorizes coercive economic measures

definitions.meaning: penalties such as trade embargoes imposed on a country

explanation.surface: Officially permits forceful trade penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means approves officially; the noun is used for trade penalties imposed on states.

clue.text: Certain to ring Vivian last

indicators.note: to ring means to encircle, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: sure means certain
Viv is a short form of the name Vivian

explanation.surface: Someone is bound to phone Vivian at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like phoning, but it means surround; 'last' is the verb, to endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to keep going, to endure or remain alive.

clue.text: A relative twice rebuffed by Heather

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for twice is read backwards

parts.note: bis is Latin (and musical) for twice, as in an encore
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A family member has been rejected two times by a woman called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns BIS (twice, as called for an encore) into SIB; Heather is the plant, ling, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother or sister is a close family member, a relative sharing parents.

clue.text: Brief trip to Australia by a philosopher

parts.note: a spin is a short drive or outing
Oz is a slang name for Australia

explanation.surface: A thinker takes a quick journey down under.
explanation.walkthrough: Spinoza was a 17th-century Dutch rationalist thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Baruch Spinoza was a Dutch rationalist thinker of the 1600s.

clue.text: Since being retired, has become established

indicators.note: being here means sitting within, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to have retired is to have gone to bed
as can mean since, because

explanation.surface: Since retiring, someone has settled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' suggests leaving work, but here it means gone to bed; 'being' is the containment signal, one word sitting within the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something based somewhere is set up or located there, settled.

clue.text: Ambushed whilst travelling by carriage

definitions.meaning: caught out by a sudden attack
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Someone was waylaid while riding in a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught by surprise means being snared; riding in a light pony cart also fits literally.

clue.text: Succeeded in making daughter admit being demoralised

parts.note: got as in managed to, succeeded in
to own (up) is to admit

explanation.surface: Someone managed to get their daughter to confess to feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling depressed or dispirited is being brought low.

clue.text: About to get slimmer daily

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
leaner means slimmer, thinner

explanation.surface: Someone is about to grow thinner each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' is a noun here: in Britain a daily is a woman who comes in each day to clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily in British usage is a domestic help who comes to tidy the house every day.

clue.text: Very little time this month

explanation.surface: Barely any time remains in the present month.
explanation.walkthrough: Formal letters once dated things 'the 5th inst.', meaning the fifth of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment is very little time, and in old business letters inst. (instant) means of the current month.

clue.text: It's not vulgar or corrupt

definitions.meaning: a coarse, colloquial contraction of it is not, written with apostrophes
to corrupt is to spoil or contaminate

explanation.surface: Something claims to be neither coarse nor crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken slangily, it is not becomes a two-apostrophe contraction; the verb also means to contaminate or spoil.

clue.text: Fully prepared to give an indication of purpose

definitions.meaning: in order means arranged and ready, with to following
the phrase introduces an aim, as in 'he left early so as to catch the train'

explanation.surface: Being fully ready serves to signal what you intend.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two parts it says things are ready and tidy; as one phrase it introduces the aim of an action, meaning so as to.

clue.text: I sound irritated by its ugly appearance

indicators.note: sound tells us the word I is replaced by something said the same way

parts.note: the letter I is pronounced like the organ of sight
sore means irritated, inflamed

explanation.surface: Someone sounds annoyed by how ugly something looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' turns I into EYE, its homophone; 'its' just ties the definition on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsightly that offends the view, such as a hideous building, is a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Misbehave on returning to create an effect

parts.note: to act up is to behave badly

indicators.note: returning means the little word comes back the other way

parts.note: the printed word should be no for the reversal to give the final letters

explanation.surface: Someone behaves badly, and turning back has some effect.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's slip: 'returning' reverses the printed 'on' into NO, but the answer ends in ON, so the clue should read 'no'. ACT UP (misbehave) comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To influence or have an effect on something is to work on it, to affect it.

clue.text: Got up and dressed

explanation.surface: Someone rose from bed and put clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb can mean rose or showed up; a smartly clad person is said to be well so.

clue.text: He charges to bill to employer

parts.note: acc. is short for account, a bill
a user is one who employs or makes use of something

explanation.surface: A man sends an invoice to the company he works for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charges' means brings charges against, not sends bills; 'employer' is just one who uses.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings a charge against another person is the one who blames them.

clue.text: Headgear hidden by one's faithful friend

indicators.note: hidden by means a word is concealed inside another

parts.note: aces are ones in cards, so one's reads as aces
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A loyal companion is hiding a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cards an ace counts as one, so 'one's' is read as a plural. Achates was the loyal companion of Aeneas in Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid he is Aeneas's loyal companion, so his name means a devoted friend.

clue.text: Cryptic jargon about a German analgesic

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a code is cryptic language
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: Obscure jargon about a German painkiller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the definition of a secret language; 'about' signals the surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an opiate painkiller derived from morphine.

clue.text: Looks at red rags being torn up

indicators.note: being torn up means the letters of red rags are ripped apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone watches red rags being ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being torn up' rearranges RED RAGS.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it or consider it.

clue.text: Two dogs get cut down

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
to tail someone is to dog them, follow closely

explanation.surface: A pair of dogs are given a reduced ration.
explanation.walkthrough: The second dog is the verb, as in to dog someone's steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To curtail is to shorten or reduce something, a synonym for cut down.

clue.text: French painter displays asperity after tea

indicators.note: after places the bitter piece after the drink

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
gall means bitterness, harshness

explanation.surface: A painter from France shows harshness following tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Marc Chagall was a Russian-born French painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marc Chagall was a Russian-born artist who worked in France.

clue.text: Annie is awfully silly

indicators.note: awfully means the letters of annie is are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Annie is very foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges ANNIE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish behaviour is described by this word, which originally meant donkey-like.

clue.text: Member needs a supporter -quite rightly

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: An MP needs a backer, quite properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a club or parliament, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting within the law means acting properly, in a lawful manner.

clue.text: Hotheaded youth leader destroyed a garden shrub

parts.note: the head of the word hot is its first letter

indicators.note: the leader of the word youth is its opening letter
destroyed means the letters of a garden are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An impetuous young ringleader wrecked a flowering bush in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotheaded' gives H, the head of hot; 'destroyed' turns A GARDEN into DRANGEA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a flowering bush with large round heads of blooms, popular in borders.

clue.text: Acknowledge that a doctor reflected on it

indicators.note: reflected means turned as in a mirror, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: MD stands for Doctor of Medicine

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that a doctor thought about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' looks like thought, but it turns MD into DM.
explanation.definitionFit: To acknowledge is to confess or concede, a synonym.

clue.text: English sovereign making ends meet

parts.note: a king is a sovereign, a monarch

explanation.surface: An English monarch is struggling to pay the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' could be the gold coin, but here it is the ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Eking out a living means getting by on scant means, just about managing.

clue.text: Better-shaped shaver

definitions.meaning: a device or person that clips hair, as a beard clipper

explanation.surface: A neater figure belongs to someone who uses a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: More neatly cut or slimmer is the comparative of the adjective trim; a clipper for beards is also one.

clue.text: Hardly likely to join a party at the club

parts.note: a social is an informal party held by a club or society

explanation.surface: Someone is unlikely to attend a club party.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the opening phrase; the rest builds A plus SOCIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsociable person who avoids company is unlikely to become a member of anything.

clue.text: Hustles corrupt detectives

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of hustles are spoiled and reordered

explanation.surface: Crooked officers are hassling private investigators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges HUSTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Investigators who track down clues are known informally by this word.

clue.text: Let Tory organise a money-making venture

indicators.note: organise means the letters of let tory are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A political party is allowed to run a fundraising scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organise' rearranges LET TORY; a Tory is a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw selling tickets for prizes raises funds for its organiser, as the National Lottery does.
